tools.name: quick_read
tools.description: Run SimianX's four live AI agents once on a US stock or a crypto pair: Fundamental reads the business or the coin, Indicator the chart, Intelligence the news flow, and Decision turns it into a call with entry, stop and target and the next candle close. Returns a run id right away; each agent's resul

tools.name: get_quick_read
tools.description: Status and results so far of a quick read. Pass wait (up to 25 s): the answer returns as soon as one more agent has finished; call again while status is queued or running, relaying each new agent.

tools.name: list_live_sessions
tools.description: The account's live analysis sessions: symbol, timeframe, since when, next run, last decision.

tools.name: get_live_session
tools.description: One live analysis session: status, next run time and the latest results.

tools.name: update_live_session
tools.description: Switch the models of a running live analysis session when the user asks; the next analysis runs on them. Their saved setup (get_settings) stays as it is.

tools.name: stop_live_session
tools.description: End a live analysis session when the user stops watching the symbol, so no more runs are charged. Safe to call twice.

tools.name: get_updates
tools.description: Every update of this key the user has not been told: finished analysis steps, decisions (with the question to ask), matched news. Relay each `say` (and `ask`) in order, then call again with ack set to the last id you relayed; unacked updates come back until you do. Use wait (up to 25 s) to hold for

tools.name: run_live_analysis
tools.description: Deprecated, sunset 2027-06-01: the same one-pass run as quick_read under its old name. Use quick_read. (uses points, metered on the models used like the website; deprecated (use /v1/analysis/quick))

tools.name: get_live_analysis
tools.description: Deprecated, sunset 2027-06-01: status and results of a run started with run_live_analysis. Use get_quick_read. (deprecated (use /v1/analysis/quick/{id}))

tools.name: get_news
tools.description: The scored news stream behind Market Pulse: every article tagged with the symbols it moves, its value (low, medium, high) and its sentiment. Newest first (with since: oldest first). Use since to fetch only what is new, cursor for older pages. (0.5 points per call)

tools.name: get_news_article
tools.description: One article from get_news with its text, symbols, value and sentiment. (0.2 points per call)

tools.name: watch_news
tools.description: Keep matching scored news for symbols server side, also while you are offline; each matching story arrives in get_updates with a sentence to relay (high-value ones ask whether to run a quick read). Several sources of one story arrive once. (needs the starter plan or above)

tools.name: list_news_watches
tools.description: The key's news watches. (needs the starter plan or above)

tools.name: stop_news_watch
tools.description: Stop matching news for a watch. (needs the starter plan or above)

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: Webhooks that receive this account's updates, with their health: check before creating one, so the user does not get every update twice.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: POST every update (or the kinds listed) to a URL, signed with HMAC-SHA256 (X-SimianX-Signature), with retries. For the user's own code (Starter plan and above); an agent that reads get_updates does not need one.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete a webhook when the user no longer wants updates pushed to that url. Cannot be undone; deliveries stop at once.

tools.name: test_webhook
tools.description: POST a signed test event to the webhook now, right after creating or changing one, to confirm the user's endpoint receives and verifies it.

tools.name: get_pulse_events
tools.description: Market Pulse events on US stocks and crypto: sudden price moves and other market events, each with a severity from 1 to 4. Newest first (with since: oldest first, pass `newest` back); delayed on lower plans. (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: get_pulse_summary
tools.description: A 24-hour overview of Market Pulse. (0.2 points per call)

tools.name: start_deep_analysis
tools.description: Start the deep research committee on a stock or a coin: four analysts (fundamentals, market, news, and positioning for stocks or derivatives for crypto), a bull and a bear researcher, a research manager and a risk manager, ending in a verdict with entry, stop and target and a PDF. Takes about ten mi

tools.name: get_deep_analysis
tools.description: State, verdict and trade plan of a deep research run. Poll until status is done.

tools.name: list_deep_analyses
tools.description: The account's recent deep research runs, newest first: find an earlier run's id instead of starting (and paying for) a new one.

tools.name: ask_deep_analysis
tools.description: Ask a follow-up question about a finished deep research run; read the answers with get_deep_thread. (uses points, metered on the models used like the website)

tools.name: get_deep_thread
tools.description: Questions asked about a deep research run and the committee's answers.

tools.name: search_instruments
tools.description: Find the symbol to use: US stocks, ETFs and crypto pairs matching a name or ticker. To look up several names, pass them together in symbols (one call) instead of calling once per name.

tools.name: get_crypto_quotes
tools.description: Latest prices of the coins on the Market Pulse board (the large caps and the coins users filter on), up to 120 per call; coins it does not carry come back in `missing` (get_crypto_candles has any pair). Nothing found, nothing charged. (0.1 points per call)

tools.name: get_crypto_candles
tools.description: OHLCV candles for a coin or pair. (0.2 points per call)

tools.name: get_crypto_indicators
tools.description: Indicator snapshot (trend, momentum, levels) for a coin or pair. (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: list_sectors
tools.description: Sectors under watch with headline stats and the event types they use. (0.2 points per call)

tools.name: get_sector
tools.description: One sector: stats, the coming catalysts, recent events and the largest companies. (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: get_sector_calendar
tools.description: Dated catalysts in a sector (for biopharma: PDUFA dates, advisory committees, trial readouts, conferences). (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: get_sector_events
tools.description: Events in a sector taken from primary sources, with severity 1-4. (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: list_autopilots
tools.description: The account's autopilots: the four live agents running on a schedule.

tools.name: create_autopilot
tools.description: Run the four live agents on a symbol on a schedule, optionally letting the Decision agent manage a paper position (Starter plan and above). Runs server side, also while you are offline; every analysis, decision and position change lands in get_updates and the event log (get_autopilot_events). After

tools.name: get_autopilot
tools.description: Status and configuration of one autopilot, with its event cursor.

tools.name: update_autopilot
tools.description: Change models, intervals, language, the timing gate or AI position control. Changing the timeframe or switching AI control off closes the paper position first.

tools.name: start_autopilot
tools.description: Restart a stopped autopilot. (uses points, metered on the models used like the website)

tools.name: stop_autopilot
tools.description: Stop an autopilot when the user wants it to stop analysing (and spending points); start_autopilot restarts it. Safe to call twice. The paper book stays: an open position keeps its stop and target and a resting order can still fill; use autopilot_action close / cancel_order first if the user wants to

tools.name: get_autopilot_events
tools.description: The autopilot's event log: analyses, signals, position changes, actions. Without after you get the latest events and a cursor; pass that cursor as after (and wait, up to 25 s) to get only what happens next.

tools.name: get_autopilot_positions
tools.description: The autopilot's paper positions and their operations. Each position counts its AI 'hold' decisions and shows the latest one; include=holds lists them all (large).

tools.name: autopilot_action
tools.description: Change the autopilot's paper position by hand, always at the server's price: open, add, reduce, close, set_levels, place_order, replace_order, cancel_order, set_timeframe. Stocks are long only, and intraday stock entries need the market open.

tools.name: run_autopilot_agent
tools.description: Run one of the autopilot's agents now, outside its schedule; the result lands in the event log. (uses points, metered on the models used like the website)

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The account behind the API key: plan, limits and the key's budgets (points figures are for your own pacing; do not read them to the user unless asked).

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: The user's default setup per market (stock, crypto): each live agent's model, the timeframe and run intervals, and the deep committee's model per seat. Every analysis started without `models` runs on it. Read it when the user asks which models or timeframe their analyses use.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.description: Save the user's default models for one market, when they ask to change them: live = the four live agents, deep = the committee seats (one setting for both markets). Paid plans only. The website shows the same setup.

tools.name: get_daily_reward
tools.description: When the user asks about their free daily reward (no purchase): whether today's is still open, extra claims, the streak, when it resets (00:00 UTC) and what it can give.

tools.name: claim_daily_reward
tools.description: Claim the user's free daily reward when they ask for it ("claim my daily reward"): today's, else an extra claim. No purchase or money involved. Tell them what they got (`prize.name`, `benefits`) and their streak.

tools.name: list_rewards
tools.description: Rewards the user has received, newest first (daily rewards, streaks and others).

tools.name: help_search
tools.description: Search SimianX's help center when the user asks how something works on the website (live analysis, deep analysis, autopilots, auto digest, points, plans, account). Returns titles, summaries and the page URL; read the full article with help_read. Without `q` it lists the articles.

tools.name: help_read
tools.description: One help center article as Markdown (category and slug from help_search). Answer from it and give the user its `url`.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: Models that can be set per agent: rates, typical points of a live call, where each applies, and `min_plan` (free accounts run gpt-6-luna; starter and above pick any listed model).

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Tell the SimianX team about a bug, missing data or an idea. Read by people; not answered.

tools.name: pricing_get
tools.description: Prices in points, plans and limits (machine readable)

tools.name: skill_get
tools.description: Skill and API versions, changelog, deprecations (read at the start of a session)

tools.name: usage_get
tools.description: Calls and points spent, broken down by key and endpoint, over the last 1-31 days: use when the user asks where their points went.

tools.name: feedback_list
tools.description: Your last 20 feedback messages (status only; we do not reply)

tools.name: quote_post
tools.description: Estimate how many points a SimianX call would cost before running it (pass the endpoint key, e.g. deep.create, and its options). Not a market price quote.

tools.name: market_status
tools.description: Whether the US stock market is open now, and when the current or next session opens and closes. Check before stock analyses or autopilots that depend on market hours.

tools.name: sectors_stocks
tools.description: Constituent stocks of a sector (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: sectors_stock
tools.description: One company inside the sector: profile, tracked assets, calendar (from 90 days back), events, market-cap peers (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: sectors_event
tools.description: One event in full (summary, facts, calendar item, readiness) with related events (0.2 points per call)

tools.name: sectors_assets
tools.description: Tracked assets (drugs, products) of a sector (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: sectors_asset
tools.description: One asset: links, trials, readiness checklist, its events and calendar, the company behind it (0.3 points per call)

tools.name: sectors_follows
tools.description: The account's follows in this sector and its subscription (needs the starter plan or above)

tools.name: sectors_follow
tools.description: Follow a stock, asset or calendar item (the first follow in a sector creates an email subscription) (needs the starter plan or above)

tools.name: sectors_unfollow
tools.description: Remove a follow by id or by target key (stock:SMMT, asset:<slug>, calendar:<id>) (needs the starter plan or above)

tools.name: news_translate
tools.description: Translate up to 20 news titles into one language, e.g. before showing headlines to a user who reads another language. (1 point per call)

tools.name: analysis_quick_list
tools.description: The account's recent quick reads (analyze runs), newest first, to find an earlier result or its id without starting a new run.

tools.name: analysis_live_list
tools.description: Recent runs (deprecated (use /v1/analysis/quick))

tools.name: deep_events
tools.description: Follow a deep research run step by step: long-poll with after=<cursor>&wait=30 and relay each event's `say` to the user. Use instead of polling get_deep_analysis while the run is going.

tools.name: deep_stop
tools.description: Stop a running or queued deep research run when the user asks to cancel it or no longer needs it. It halts within a few seconds (status becomes stopped); points already used are not refunded and deep_resume can continue it later.

tools.name: deep_resume
tools.description: Continue a deep research run that is paused (points ran out), stopped or failed, from the step it reached. Check the balance first: the remaining steps are charged. (uses points, metered on the models used like the website)

tools.name: deep_pdf
tools.description: Get a download link for the PDF report of a finished deep research run (status done), to hand the user a shareable document. Free plans get a watermarked copy.

tools.name: autopilots_delete
tools.description: Archive an autopilot that is already stopped, to remove it from the list. Stop it first with stop_autopilot; its history is kept and start_autopilot brings it back. Its paper book is left as it is (close it first to be flat).

tools.name: autopilots_analyses
tools.description: Past analyses of one autopilot, newest first, filterable by agent: use to explain why the autopilot did what it did. Pass include=text for the full write-ups.

tools.name: autopilots_logs
tools.description: Lifecycle and delivery log of one autopilot (started, stopped, paused, webhook deliveries): use when an autopilot stopped unexpectedly or updates did not arrive.

tools.name: webhooks_get
tools.description: One webhook's configuration and delivery health (last success, failures), by id.

tools.name: webhooks_update
tools.description: Change a webhook's url, subscribed events, ack mode or active flag, e.g. to re-enable one that was switched off after failures.

tools.name: webhooks_failures
tools.description: The last 50 failed deliveries and dead letters of a webhook: use when the user says updates are not arriving at their endpoint.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "send_feedback" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: message, category, severity, endpoint, request_id, context, idempotency_key

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_deep_thread, help_search, help_read, feedback_list · Private data: get_account, deep_pdf · Public sink: create_webhook, delete_webhook, test_webhook, send_feedback, quote_post, sectors_follow, autopilots_logs, webhooks_get, webhooks_update, webhooks_failures · Destructive: quick_read, list_live_sessions, get_live_session, get_updates, run_live_analysis, get_live_analysis, watch_news, delete_webhook, start_deep_analysis, get_deep_analysis, list_deep_analyses, ask_deep_analysis, get_deep_thread, create_autopilot, run_autopilot_agent, get_settings, list_models, sectors_unfollow, analysis_quick_list, deep_events, deep_stop, deep_resume, deep_pdf, autopilots_delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_deep_thread, help_search, help_read, feedback_list · Private data: get_account, deep_pdf · Public sink: create_webhook, delete_webhook, test_webhook, send_feedback, quote_post, sectors_follow, autopilots_logs, webhooks_get, webhooks_update, webhooks_failures · Destructive: quick_read, list_live_sessions, get_live_session, get_updates, run_live_analysis, get_live_analysis, watch_news, delete_webhook, start_deep_analysis, get_deep_analysis, list_deep_analyses, ask_deep_analysis, get_deep_thread, create_autopilot, run_autopilot_agent, get_settings, list_models, sectors_unfollow, analysis_quick_list, deep_events, deep_stop, deep_resume, deep_pdf, autopilots_delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
